chapter: Chicago years: recordings, Armstrong, wartime exit
title: Decca sessions in Chicago and New York, 1936-38
summary: After Decca recording in Chicago, the band went to New York in 1938 for a three-day session when the Chicago Decca studio was closed. Then he returned to Chicago.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, in 1936, Herb, as you said before, you recorded for Deck of Records. That was in Chicago.

Yeah, in Chicago. And then we had a session in New York in 1938. That's where we made the Viper song. If you were Viper, we left Chicago and went to New York. We made those records in New York at a three session. We stood there for about three days.
I see, and that was the only time you were in New York up until about 1941 or 42, wasn't it?
Yeah, you know, before I played at Capital Palace.
Yeah. And what were some of your other dates, or where else did you play between 1936 and 1940, or about 41?

I came back to Chicago, you see, after I left New York. I was stationed there in Chicago, but we just went to New York for that recording session. On top of the Decker studio had moved, discontinued in Chicago for the time being. So we had to go to New York to make the Decker records.
